title: Content-driven Style control cadence
purpose: Finish the Elementor editor behavior where Content filter composition drives Style controls.
objective: Make type-specific Style sections appear only for active filter types without adding a separate builder UI.
scope_boundary: In scope: editor hidden type flags, Style section conditions, Range/Rating section separation, documentation, and mechanical verification. Out of scope: deep per-type style expansion, browser-heavy Elementor QA, preset-owned Style settings, or frontend filtering runtime changes.
entry_condition: TASK-FC-020 is done and the plugin worktree is clean.
exit_condition: Content filter types drive the visible Style sections consistently enough for Guilherme to QA in Elementor.
completion_criteria: Filter type flags recalculate from widget settings even when Content controls are not visible.
Range controls are isolated to a Range section.
Rating controls are isolated to a Rating section.
The existing option/field/global Style sections continue using native Elementor conditions.
No new custom editor UI framework is introduced.

phases.title: State sync
phases.purpose: Make editor helper flags follow the actual repeater settings.

phases.title: Style sections
phases.purpose: Split type-specific sections so labels match the active type.

phases.title: Verification
phases.purpose: Run syntax checks and record the visual QA boundary.

acceptance_criteria: Implementation follows the Content decides Style rule from docs/implementation-toolkit/filter-controller-widget-first-agentic-plan.md.
No plugin source outside editor JS and Elementor Style controls is changed unless verification proves it necessary.
Guilherme remains responsible for multi-click Elementor visual QA.
verification: Plugin PHP lint, Composer validation, JS syntax check, and diff checks pass.
stop_conditions: The fix requires unsupported Elementor internals beyond the existing editor settings command fallback.
The change starts adding deep type styling unrelated to section cadence.
